instagram_caption:
Quentin Tarantino's film school was a video store. 📼

A high school dropout, he spent about five years in the 1980s clerking at Video Archives in Manhattan Beach, California. He talked movies all day, with customers and with a co-worker named Roger Avary. (He says he was already a movie expert. That's how he got the job.)

Then came Reservoir Dogs (1992) and Pulp Fiction: the 1994 Palme d'Or and the Oscar for Best Original Screenplay, shared with Avary.

When the store closed, Tarantino bought its tape library. He has put his collection at close to 8,000 tapes and DVDs. Since 2022 he and Avary have been rewatching them, cassette by cassette, on The Video Archives Podcast.

The twist: the video store clerk now owns two Los Angeles cinemas. The New Beverly (bought 2007, programmed by him since 2014) and the Vista (reopened 2023) project film prints only, many at the New Bev from his own collection.

He came up on tape. Now he's keeping film running.
